about: The core set of buildings (decision 'Playable 32': a core set). cost: talents; years: to build; upkeep: talents a year; max: how many times it can be built in one province; needs: river (a river or floodplain), hills, ore (a mineral deposit), coast, town (10,000 people or more in the province's largest place). effects: field, orchard, mine, gather (production of that kind of work in the province, as a share more), famine (share of a bad harvest's loss it saves), crafts (made goods), trade (goods value and customs), ships (warship cost for the realm), integration (speed), unrest (added), garrison (Might added to the walls), manpower (the province's levies), growth (the region's Health growth factor, weighted by the province's people). Our own data, free for any use. requires: a technology the realm must know to build it. levels: each level's name; a building can be raised to its last level, each level costing its cost times the level and taking its years; effects count once per level. good:<id>: that good's output in the province (land goods) or the realm's output of it weighted by the province's people (made goods), as a share more per level. research: the realm's research, as a share, weighted by the province's people. storage: stores of goods (their use waits on the Ledger's 'Stores of goods'). needs has:<good>: the province must yield that good. The Ledger topic 'Buildings and works' (your answer 'Much more than either choice, almost one for each resource, manufactured, intermediate, alongside other buildings like storage and ones that have various effects').

buildings.name: Irrigation works
buildings.description: Canals, dykes and water-lifting wheels: fields that drink when the rain fails. Needs a river or floodplain.

buildings.name: Granary
buildings.description: Stored grain: a bad harvest hurts half as much.

buildings.name: Terraces
buildings.description: Walled steps on the hillsides for vines and olives. Needs hilly land.

buildings.name: Mines
buildings.description: Shafts, adits and washing floors: half again as much ore and stone. Needs a deposit.

buildings.name: Workshops
buildings.description: Potteries, forges, fulling mills and looms: the province makes more of every made good.

buildings.name: Market and fora
buildings.description: A market square with weights and measures: more trade, and more customs from it.

buildings.name: Harbour
buildings.description: Moles, quays and shipsheds: more fishing and trade, and warships a quarter cheaper for the realm. Needs a coast.

buildings.name: Roads
buildings.description: Paved roads and bridges: the province settles into the realm faster, and goods move.

buildings.name: City walls
buildings.description: Stone walls and towers: besiegers take longer. Can be built twice.

buildings.name: Barracks and drill fields
buildings.description: A place to train: more of the province's men can be called up.

buildings.name: Great temple
buildings.description: A great sanctuary to the gods of the province's people: less unrest, and they accept you sooner.

buildings.name: Aqueduct and baths
buildings.description: Clean water for a crowded town: healthier people and a contented city. Needs a town of some size.

buildings.name: Grain estates
buildings.description: Great farms of wheat and barley, worked by tenants and the enslaved, like the latifundia of Italy and Sicily.

buildings.name: Bean and lentil fields
buildings.description: Fields of lentils, chickpeas, peas and beans: the poor man's meat.

buildings.name: Flax fields
buildings.description: Watered fields of flax and hemp for linen and rope; Egypt's linen was famous.

buildings.name: Sesame fields
buildings.description: Sesame for oil, grown along the Nile and in Mesopotamia.

buildings.name: Olive groves
buildings.description: Olive trees take years to bear; then they give oil for food, lamps and the baths.

buildings.name: Vineyards
buildings.description: Vines for wine: Chian, Falernian, Thasian were prized by name.

buildings.name: Fruit orchards
buildings.description: Figs, dates, pomegranates and nuts.

buildings.name: Market gardens
buildings.description: Gardens of vegetables and herbs around a town.

buildings.name: Cattle ranches
buildings.description: Herds of cattle for ploughing, milk, hides and meat.

buildings.name: Sheep runs
buildings.description: Flocks for wool, moving between summer and winter pastures.

buildings.name: Goat herds
buildings.description: Goats for milk, cheese and hides on rough land.

buildings.name: Pig farms
buildings.description: Pigs fed in oak woods and on scraps.

buildings.name: Horse studs
buildings.description: Breeding horses for cavalry and chariots, like the royal studs of Media and Thessaly.

buildings.name: Camel herds
buildings.description: Camels for the desert caravans.

buildings.name: Poultry yards
buildings.description: Hens, ducks and geese for the town markets.

buildings.name: Fisheries
buildings.description: Boats, nets and tuna watches along the coast.

buildings.name: Apiaries
buildings.description: Beehives for honey and wax.

buildings.name: Reed beds
buildings.description: Reeds and papyrus cut in the marshes and along the rivers.

buildings.name: Herb gatherers
buildings.description: Gatherers of healing herbs for the physicians.

buildings.name: Resin tappers
buildings.description: Tapping pines for resin and boiling pitch for ships and wine jars.

buildings.name: Murex fisheries
buildings.description: Diving for murex shells for the purple dye of Tyre.

buildings.name: Incense groves
buildings.description: Tending the trees of frankincense and myrrh, the wealth of Arabia Felix.

buildings.name: Ivory hunters
buildings.description: Hunting elephants for their tusks.

buildings.name: Silphium gatherers
buildings.description: Cyrene's silphium, so prized it was gathered to extinction by Nero's day.

buildings.name: Logging camps
buildings.description: Woodcutters and their mules.

buildings.name: Ship-timber forests
buildings.description: Tall straight trees for masts and keels: Macedon's firs, Lebanon's cedars.

buildings.name: Charcoal burners
buildings.description: Earth-covered kilns turning wood to charcoal for the smiths.

buildings.name: Quarries
buildings.description: Cutting stone: Pentelic and Carrara marble, Egyptian granite and porphyry.

buildings.name: Clay pits
buildings.description: Digging clay and sand for potters, brick-makers and glass-makers.

buildings.name: Iron mines
buildings.description: Iron ore: Noricum, Elba, the Chalybes.

buildings.name: Copper mines
buildings.description: Copper and tin for bronze: Cyprus, Spain, Cornwall's tin by sea.

buildings.name: Silver mines
buildings.description: Silver and lead: Laurion, the Spanish mines of New Carthage.

buildings.name: Gold mines
buildings.description: Gold washed from rivers and dug from the hills: Thrace, Spain, Nubia.

buildings.name: Salt pans
buildings.description: Evaporating sea water for salt, to keep fish and meat.

buildings.name: Mineral works
buildings.description: Sulfur, alum, natron and bitumen for dyers, glass-makers and builders.

buildings.name: Turquoise mines
buildings.description: Sinai's turquoise.

buildings.name: Mills and bakeries
buildings.description: Querns, donkey mills and bakeries feeding the towns.

buildings.name: Breweries
buildings.description: Beer for Egypt, Mesopotamia and the Celts.

buildings.name: Garum works
buildings.description: Salting fish and making garum, the fish sauce of the Mediterranean.

buildings.name: Potteries
buildings.description: Wheel-thrown pots, amphorae for wine and oil, and fine painted ware.

buildings.name: Brickworks
buildings.description: Kilns for bricks and roof tiles.

buildings.name: Lime kilns
buildings.description: Burning limestone for mortar and plaster.

buildings.name: Oil presses
buildings.description: Lever and screw presses for oil.

buildings.name: Wine presses
buildings.description: Treading floors and presses for wine.

buildings.name: Drying sheds
buildings.description: Drying figs, dates and raisins, and boiling fruit in honey.

buildings.name: Spinning houses
buildings.description: Retting flax and spinning yarn, the work of every household.

buildings.name: Weaving houses
buildings.description: Looms for linen and wool.

buildings.name: Ropewalks
buildings.description: Rope and sailcloth for the fleets.

buildings.name: Dye works
buildings.description: Vats of madder, woad and murex.

buildings.name: Smelters
buildings.description: Furnaces turning ore into metal.

buildings.name: Smithies
buildings.description: Smiths hammering iron into tools and nails.

buildings.name: Bronze foundries
buildings.description: Casting bronze: statues, vessels, fittings.

buildings.name: Armouries
buildings.description: Making swords, spears, helmets and mail for the armies.

buildings.name: Stonemasons' yards
buildings.description: Dressing stone for temples, walls and roads.

buildings.name: Carpenters' yards
buildings.description: Sawing and joining timber.

buildings.name: Cartwrights
buildings.description: Carts, wheels and harness.

buildings.name: Shipyards
buildings.description: Slipways and sheds for building ships, like Carthage's round harbour.

buildings.name: Perfumeries
buildings.description: Blending incense and perfume: Capua, Alexandria.

buildings.name: Glassworks
buildings.description: Sidon's glass-blowers.

buildings.name: Papyrus and parchment works
buildings.description: Papyrus from Egypt; parchment from Pergamon.

buildings.name: Goldsmiths and carvers
buildings.description: Jewellery, worked ivory and fine things for the rich.

buildings.name: Warehouses
buildings.description: Storehouses for grain, metal and timber (their full use waits on stores of goods).

buildings.name: Library
buildings.description: Scrolls and scholars: research grows.

buildings.name: Schools
buildings.description: Teachers of letters and the gymnasium: research and integration.

buildings.name: Baths
buildings.description: Public baths: cleaner and calmer towns.

buildings.name: Theatre
buildings.description: Plays and festivals calm the town.

buildings.name: Mint
buildings.description: Striking coin locally: trade flows easier.

buildings.name: Agora and forum
buildings.description: The meeting place of the town: courts, assemblies, shops.
